# Technical Specification — AI-Driven FinOps & Cost Optimization — Technical Specification

## Architecture
Event-driven microservices on Kubernetes. All services expose gRPC internally
and REST/JSON externally. Schema registry enforces contract compatibility.

## Technology Stack
MLOps pipelines (Kubeflow/MLflow), developer experience AI (Copilot-class code intelligence), observability stack (OpenTelemetry + PromQL), and policy-as-code governance

## Data Architecture
**Primary:** PostgreSQL 16 (application data) + ClickHouse (analytics/telemetry) + Redis Cluster (rate limiting/caching)
**Cache:** Redis Cluster (read-through, write-behind)
**Search:** Elasticsearch 8 (BM25 + kNN hybrid)
**Streaming:** Apache Kafka (3-node, RF=3, ISR=2)

## Security Controls
| Control | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| AuthN | OAuth 2.0 + OIDC (RS256 JWT) |
| AuthZ | RBAC + ABAC via OPA Gatekeeper |
| Encryption at rest | AES-256-GCM (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) |
| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.3 (mTLS service-to-service) |
| Secrets management | HashiCorp Vault (dynamic credentials) |
| Vulnerability scanning | Trivy (container) + Dependabot (deps) |

## Scalability Targets
- Throughput: 50,000 req/min sustained
- Latency: p50 ≤ 80ms · p95 ≤ 150ms · p99 ≤ 200ms
- Availability: 99.95% monthly SLA
- Storage: petabyte-scale object storage for model artefacts

## CI/CD Pipeline
GitHub Actions → unit tests → integration tests → container build →
SAST/DAST scan → staging deploy → smoke tests → production canary (5% → 100%)

structured.title: AI-Driven FinOps & Cost Optimization — Technical Specification
structured.goal: Ensure all Lead Engineers and Architects understand and align with the proposed data pipeline architecture for AI-driven FinOps. This includes clarity on data ingestion, ML model integration, and recommendation enforcement mechanisms, fostering a unified development approach.
structured.blueprintContext:
The AI-Driven FinOps & Cost Optimization system analyzes cloud spending patterns using machine learning to identify anomalies and recommend or automatically implement cost-saving actions.

The primary actor (FinOps Engineer/Cloud Administrator) flow involves: 1. Ingesting cloud billing data from Azure APIs. 2. Reviewing AI-generated cost optimization recommendations. 3. Approving or configuring automated policy enforcement for actions like rightsizing or reserved instance purchasing.

Key non-functional targets include near real-time processing for recommendations, 99.99% availability, and sub-second response times for the recommendation engine API.
